title: Instant Graph Neural Networks for Dynamic Graphs

problem.claim: Instantly representing continuous changes in large-scale dynamic graphs with GNNs remains an open problem.

gap.claim: Existing dynamic GNNs commonly model periodic graph evolution on snapshots, causing delayed representation updates and costly recomputation over the entire graph.

contributions.claim: InstantGNN uses incremental computation to update the graph representation matrix for dynamic graphs.
The method supports edge-arrival dynamic graphs with instant representation updates and predictions, and supports dynamic structures and dynamic attributes.
Upper bounds for the time complexity of the updates are provided.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method is reported to avoid repetitive computations and enable instant updates and predictions for edge-arrival dynamic graphs.
The authors report experiments on several real-world and synthetic datasets.
The authors report state-of-the-art accuracy and orders-of-magnitude higher efficiency than existing methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for graph-structured data, and recent work has improved their scalability to graphs with millions of nodes.
Instant representation of continuous changes in large-scale dynamic graphs remains unresolved.
Snapshot-oriented dynamic GNNs delay change propagation and repeatedly recompute representations for the entire graph.
InstantGNN applies incremental computation, supports dynamic structures and attributes, provides update complexity bounds, and adaptively schedules retraining.
Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets are reported to show high accuracy and substantially higher efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Snapshot-based processing delays representation changes and repeatedly recomputes the entire graph.

interpretation.claim: When graph changes arrive continuously, incremental updates may better align computation with the timing and locality of changes.

application.claim: For edge-arrival dynamic graph systems, consider incremental representation updates and prediction paths.

exception.claim: The abstract specifically describes the edge-arrival model; applicability to other change models is not established.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings.
Exact update time-complexity bounds and retraining policy details are not provided.
